Hi [~accountid:5b8d306bfa38ae2c89608b95] please see below my inicial thoughts:

*Question 1: Alcohol advertising in PT. What is allowed & not allowed in the market?*

All forms of hidden, indirect or malicious advertising are prohibited in accordance of article 60 Portuguese Constitution in Portugal. 

The Advertising Code (Article 17) includes limitations on alcohol advertising, which is only possible when: 

* It is not aimed specifically at minors and, in particular, does not show them consuming such beverages;
* it does not encourage excessive consumption
* it does not disparage non-consumers
* it does not suggest success, social success or special abilities as a result of consumption;
* Does not suggest the existence, in alcoholic beverages, of therapeutic properties or of stimulant or sedative effects;
* It does not associate the consumption of these beverages with physical exercise or driving
* It does not emphasise the alcohol content of the beverages as a positive quality.

Additionally, it is forbidden to:

* advertise alcoholic beverages on television and radio between 7 a.m. and 10:30pm 
* associate the advertising of alcoholic beverages to national symbols, enshrined in Article 11 of the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic.
* commercial communications and advertising of any events in which minors participate, namely sports, cultural, recreational or other activities, shall not display or make any mention, implicit or explicit, of the brand or brands of alcoholic beverages ( No alcoholic beverage brands shall be displayed or in any way advertised at these locations)

Furthermore, there are codes of conducts to be aware of depending on the type of beverage:

# for beers: [https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/CODIGO-DE-AUTORREGULACAO-DOS-CERVEJEIROS-PORTUGUESES-PARA-A-COMUNICACAO-COMERCIAL.pdf|https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/CODIGO-DE-AUTORREGULACAO-DOS-CERVEJEIROS-PORTUGUESES-PARA-A-COMUNICACAO-COMERCIAL.pdf]
# Wine and spirits: [https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Codigo_BebidasAlcoolicas_Vinhos_Espirituosas.pdf|https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Codigo_BebidasAlcoolicas_Vinhos_Espirituosas.pdf]

 *Question 2: Can we do some banner to increase visibility inside of the Bolt Food marketplace or on the provider level? What should be some of the measures or message on the ad to make it in compliance with the law?*

The add would need to comply with the regulations above. There are some unclarity in relation to timing: would in the case of digital marketing we require to comply with the timeframe: no banner between 7am and 10:30pm? Moreover, how could you add the indication “SEJA RESPONSÁVEL. BEBA COM MODERAÇÃO”?

Thanks for the feedback from the Partner on this.

I would like to highlight that both Bolt and the Partner are considered separate data controllers according to the GDPR's definition. Each controller has their own responsibilities regarding the processing of personal data as mandated by the GDPR. Bolt still retains the same obligations in relation to this data as imposed by the GDPR.

The reason our Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) specifies the obligations of the Partner is because Bolt shares personal data with them. By reiterating in the DSA that the Partner must comply with the law, we ensure that both parties recognize their responsibilities in handling this shared data. It's important to note that this agreement pertains to privacy laws rather than commercial ones, so the obligations cannot be biased. Privacy laws require all parties involved to assume responsibility for data processing.

*Sharing of names:* It is not possible for us to cease sharing the client's name, courier's name, and phone number. This is because Bolt acts as a marketplace facilitating the connection between the Partner and the end-user. When a user places an order, the processing of the order and other related details are governed by the agreement for the sale of goods entered into between the end-user and the partner.

Below you can find the Memorandum that explains our roles and other details pertaining to data sharing.

{noformat}SELECT 
  /*+ IGNORE_PLAN_CACHE() */
  pr.ride_fee_amount + pr.toll_road_amount + pr.booking_fee_amount AS total,
  pr.currency AS currency,
  pr.date AS date,
  pr.ride_fee_amount AS ride_fee_amount,
  pr.toll_road_amount AS toll_road_amount,
  pr.booking_fee_amount AS booking_fee_amount
FROM (
    SELECT
      /*+ IGNORE_PLAN_CACHE() */
      kv.currency AS currency,
      DATE_FORMAT(
        CONVERT_TZ(kv.action_timestamp, 'UTC', 'Europe/Warsaw'),
        '%Y-%m-%d'
      ) AS `date`,
      SUM(kv.ride_fee_amount) AS ride_fee_amount,
      SUM(kv.toll_road_amount) AS toll_road_amount,
      SUM(kv.booking_fee_amount) AS booking_fee_amount
    FROM (
        SELECT
          /*+ IGNORE_PLAN_CACHE() */
          opt.currency AS currency,
          opt.action_timestamp as action_timestamp,
          opt.ride_fee_amount AS ride_fee_amount,
          opt.toll_road_amount AS toll_road_amount,
          opt.booking_fee_amount AS booking_fee_amount,
          trim(opt.payment_method_type) AS payment_method_type,
          trim(opt.payment_method_id) AS payment_method_id
        FROM
          `order_pricing_transaction` AS opt
        WHERE
          opt.action_timestamp >= FROM_UNIXTIME(1669413600)
          AND opt.action_timestamp < FROM_UNIXTIME(1670018400)
          AND opt.driver_id = 1503441
    ) kv
    WHERE COALESCE(kv.payment_method_type, 'default') NOT IN ('default', 'corporate_ext')
    AND COALESCE(kv.payment_method_id, 'cash') != 'cash'
    GROUP BY 
      kv.currency, kv.action_timestamp
    ORDER BY
      kv.action_timestamp
) pr{noformat}

For future reference, the PR here contains some useful discussion about setting timeouts: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/68582|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/68582|smart-link] 

Some conclusions:

* Use the p99 measured from the client’s point of view when looking at the distribution of latencies on the server side, not for all the callers of the endpoint.
* Use 70% of the timeout value for the warning limit, using as inspiration the NJSC default for cron timeouts.
* As a rule of thumb, use a multiplier of the p99 of an endpoint when setting its timeout, between 1.5x and 4x. Went here with 3x.

This profiling runs on a multitude of things from devices, payment methods, domains etc. So a lot of risk indicators that compile a fraud score. We’ve got a bunch of reports where the user wasn’t redirected to the active order (AO) screen once the order was placed. After multiple investigations we realised that the basket data served through polling is filtered by the created timestamp to the last day (more recently updated to two days, during the schedule order developments). This is leaving room for old baskets to “magically” disappear from polling.

How to reproduce:

* create basket
* let it get old (active baskets are served if they have been updated in the last 48 hours, so one can update the basket every 20 hours and end up with a really old basket, X days old)
* place an order with this basket
* observe the polling response (basket data is missing)

This is how the email validations currently works:

* we do full email validation (basic format check + call to {{/internal/verifyEmail}} (does ip score on the email domain) + call to {{/internal/getEmailBlockStatus}}) when we decide whether or not to start the email OTP process for the user (rather than just archiving the old user)
* we don’t do any email validations on getAppState calls (when calculating the {{verification_options}} field), as an invalid email may cause a bad user experience and may crash the app. 
* we do only basic validation (basic format check + call to {{/internal/verifyEmail}}) on startEmailValidation (right before emailing the otp)

Basically, from the point of view of {{/internal/getEmailBlockStatus}}, we call it after confirmPhoneVerification, when deciding whether or not to start the email OTP flow, and once this decision has been made we stick with it until the end of the flow (or until the provisional login expires - 24hrs), even if the email has been market as bouncy in the meanwhile. This is to preserve a good user experience.

We may wish to revisit this behaviour after the email OTP test is finished.

[~accountid:61e55b5bfd5a690068af99d2] [~accountid:5fedbf73f7ea2a01077a3dd8] About question 2., we have some first results on a simulated grid city (20km x 20km) with orders and drivers distributed as shown in the plot:

!Screenshot 2023-06-20 at 17.56.46.png|width=75%!

Each run simulates 10 minutes of activity, with 50 drivers initially available, and orders being created and new drivers becoming available both at a rate of 10/sec. Each driver has a fixed response time of 10 seconds and if an order doesn’t get a positive response in 2 minutes, it is cancelled. Trip lengths vary between 1km and 30km. Drivers' preferences for maximum pickup distance vary between 5km and 15km. A driver’s rejection probability increases with the ratio between pickup and trip distance.

Running 10 simulations with simple allocation of the closest available driver we get an average and standard deviation for the percentage of assigned orders  of 57.6% (0.5%).

On a second experiment we introduce a simple heuristic to try to assign further away drivers for longer trips. If the trip length is longer than 5km, priority is given to available drivers at a pickup distance between 50% and 100% of the trip length. If no such drivers exist, the closest available one is returned, as usual. The resulting distribution of percentages of finished orders is 62.1% (0.6%).

Details can be seen in this [notebook|https://github.com/bolteu/data-science-research/blob/main/driver-ordering/3.%20adaptive%20search%20simulations.ipynb].

All occurrences of {{ER_DUP entry on order activity generation}} are logged from the {{OrderActivitiesUpdaterService.ensureActivitiesExistInDBForOrder}} method. 

The function checks if a row exists for an order id in the DB. If the row doesn’t exist, it inserts it. 

At first glance this looks like a race condition where the process sees that the row doesn’t exist, starts to generate the row (which is a heavy operation involving multiple API and DB calls), but by the time it finished generating them and it tries to insert into the table, there is a row already inserted by another process.

Some possible solutions: wrap the checking and insertion in a transaction, replace the final insert with an {{insert ignore}}, replace the final insert with an {{insert on duplicate key update}}

Consumers can use the ODR platform to:

* *request direct talks*, i.e. contact the trader and potentially resolve the dispute directly; or
* *submit a complaint against the trader* and *agree on an out‑of‑court dispute resolution body* to resolve the consumer dispute.

*The request for direct talks* is possible if the consumer has not yet contacted the trader or if the trader is open to dialogue. In this case, the platform notifies the trader about the consumer's request. If the trader is willing to talk, the consumer and the trader are able to exchange messages and send attachments directly through the platform. They have a maximum of *90 days* to reach an agreement and may withdraw from direct talks at any time during this period. If an agreement is not reached in 90 days, the case will be automatically closed on the platform.

The consumer can also use the platform to solve problems with the help of an approved out‑of‑court dispute resolution body by *submitting a complaint.* In this case, the platform notifies the trader about the complaint. If the trader agrees to use the ODR process, then both parties have to agree on an out‑of‑court dispute resolution body to handle their case. The parties have *30 days* from submitting the complaint to agreeing on an out‑of‑court dispute resolution body that will handle their case. If they are unable to agree on an out‑of‑court dispute resolution body in time or if the trader ignores the consumer's complaint, the procedure on the platform is terminated.

Hi [~accountid:626c24971a4eb30069d28197], 

As requested on slack, here is some further guidance on the scheduled rides feature. 

*Angle of employment risk*: Disabling a feature that allows drivers to earn more on the platform limits drivers’ right to access platform services and shows that the platform is monitoring drivers’ behaviour on the platform. Supervising the performance of work using electronic means is an element of employment.

*General approach:* To avoid the employment risk, we recommend enabling the feature for *all drivers*. This option is well defendable and even strengthens our position against reclassification risks. We will be able to say that drivers who join us to deliver transportation services may choose different ways of how to provide services on our platform, meaning there is a lot of freedom for drivers as to how they choose to use our platform. 

*Suggested approach for Finland*: As discussed earlier, you are looking to restrict the feature at least to some extent. To mitigate the employment risk and make the feature defensible to some extent, we could structure a Scheduled Rides feature for drivers as an incentive - meaning, if you do X, we enable for you a feature Y.

*Metrics used for determining whether the incentive applies*. Please note that in order for the risk to be mitigated and the feature to be defensible, the metrics used as X shall not include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *before* the driver has accepted the trip (e.g. acceptance rate). The metrics used as X, however, could include metrics that measure drivers’ performance *after* the driver has accepted the trip (e.g. completed rides, experience of driving on the platform). The metrics for performance measurement after the acceptance of the trip are defensible, since in that case drivers have already committed to the passenger to deliver him/her to the requested destination. If the driver does not honor this commitment, the driver is in breach of the contract concluded between the driver and the rider. +As I understand from our discussion on slack, you are looking to restrict it solely based on driver rating provided by the rider after a completed trip and if this description is correct then this is in line the approach described above and could therefore be tested in Finland.+ 

*Angle of transparency*. Should we opt for a restricted option as described above, we need to make it clear to the drivers that they have an opportunity to use Scheduled Rides, provided they fulfill certain criteria (e.g. have been driving on a platform for six months, have completed 100 trips etc). The transparency may be reflected on the copies or in the T&Cs and in this case I would suggest reflecting this on the copies. 

Let me know if you need additional advice. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Investigation: STK was picked up with a date 20.06 at *15:02*. First run of integration took picked pick lists between *13:02* and *15:02*. Today’s run took picked pick lists from *15:02* to *8:02*, because STK was with the time 15:02 it was included double in the integration events.



Solution: I created Calculated Field to increment “As Of Entry DateTime of Last Completed or Completed with Warnings Integration Event” with additional one minute. So schedule will pick dates 13:03 - 15:02 and then 15:03 - 8:02.

(How does it work?

We have *two timers*:

# One calculating *driver's online hours*
# The other calculating *driver's offline hours*

When the driver has an active order (picking up a customer or driving with a customer), online hours timer will increase. As soon as the driver exceeds the maximum online hours limit set in Admin, the driver gets blocked. 

When the driver takes a break (goes offline, or is blocked due to exceeding max online hours limit), the offline hour timer starts counting. If the timer exceeds the offline hours limit, the online hours timer will reset to 0, and the possible block will be removed. If the driver starts driving before the offline hours limit is reached, we continue counting online hours from the point where the online hours timer had stopped last time.

*_Note!_* _Online hours timer counts only time with an active order. So the time spent waiting between trips (driver state = waiting for orders) is not included in online hours timer._ *_Exception_*_: In Sydney and London, the online hours counter includes also driver's time spent in Waiting for orders -state._ )

# The Bolt Drive operations team must build a *solid* *business case* to support this _“commercial campaign”_. AB had a call with [~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e] on 21.06.23 to get some further background information on this ticket. 

+*Summary of discussion*+

* Bolt has applied for 70+ offices, and historically when doing so Use Class e(g)(i) is always applied for. 

*_Use Class E – Commercial, Business and Service_*

*_g) for—_*
*_(i) an office to carry out any operational or administrative functions_*

* Bolt has been able to do this as they demonstrate that the office is used for administrative purposes and this has been widely accepted without any further discussions. Sometimes Bolt are required to provide that the office is sufficiently administrative ([~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e] gave examples of how this is achieved). The issue is, there have been a few instances where planning authorities have declined Bolt using use class e(g)(i) and the rationale they give is because Bolt is a taxi business and a taxi booking office, so they say that Bolt needs to apply for Sui Generis so they are saying Bolt is Sui generis and not e(g)(i).  
* Bolt have currently accepted 3 applications (check this number with [~accountid:60528926695c3900706cc79e] ) with Sui Generis as the Use Class. 

[~accountid:60528926695c3900706cc79e] has recently successfully negotiated Chesterfield so this location is no longer affected by the Sui Generis issue. 

The operations team and licensing team would like to establish if there is a risk for Bolt accepting Sui Generis as the Use Class on any of the offices (will accepting this Use Class have an impact on any licensing requirements etc). If there is a risk should Bolt be approaching these Licensors to change the Use Class? 

{color:#008da6}+*Question on the ticket is*+{color}{color:#008da6}*:*{color} Is Sui Generis an acceptable Use Class for Bolt to use, are there any risks where Bolt have accepted Sui Generis? should Bolt be approaching these licensors to see if they will change the Use Class (with the exception of Leeds as mentioned by [~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e]). Or is is acceptable that Bolt have accepted Sui Generis? 

{color:#008da6}+*Urgency to get this work complete:*+ {color}Without knowing the risks we cannot determine what the urgency level is. 

[~accountid:629736189bc7150068ce0c0e] informed me that moving forward Bolt will always express that they want Use Class e(g)(i).

+*AB RESEARCH*+ 

Class E is a new Use Class (Commercial, Business and Service), introduced on 1st September 2020, includes a broad and diverse range of uses which principally serve the needs of visiting members of the public and or are suitable for a town centre area.

*New Class E uses benefit from permitted development rights that include:* 

* Changes to use class C3 (dwellinghouses) subject to prior approval
* Changes to a mixed use for anything within Class E and as up to two flats subject to prior approval and back again
* Change to a state funded school or back to a previous lawful use

+*INFORMATION ON SUI GENERIS*+ 

* Use class Sui Generis of the [Use Classes Order 1987|http://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1987/764/contents/made] (as amended) are all other locations which do not fit into one of the other categories, they are unique in themselves. 
* Sui Generis – Properties not fitting in any of the above categories / use classes. Meaning “of its (his, her, or their) own kind; in a class by itself; unique” 

+*Sui Generis Examples*+

_The list below is not a complete list_ 

theatres
betting offices
payday loan shops
funfairs
large houses in multiple occupation (seven or more)
‘Alkali work’ (any work registrable under the [Alkali, etc. Works Regulation Act 1906|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/Edw7/6/14/contents] (as amended)) 
hostels providing no significant element of care 
scrap yards
yard for the storage/distribution of minerals
yard for the breaking of motor vehicles
fuel stations
locations selling and / or displaying motor vehicles
retail warehouse clubs
nightclubs
launderettes
police stations 
taxi businesses
car hire locations
amusement arcades and centres
casinos
landfill sites
motorsport arenas
firearm range
postal sorting offices
public house, wine bar or drinking establishment
drinking establishment with expanded food provision
hot food takeaway where consumption is mainly away from the location of purchase
venue for live music performance
cinema
concert hall
bingo hall
dance hall

+*Implications of Sui Generis Use Class*+

* As a use class, Sui Generis properties do not automatically benefit from the permitted development rights to change to an alternative use. This is to say, a change of use from a Sui Generis use or to a Sui Generis will often be subject to full local consideration through the planning application process. 
* Even to change from one Sui Generis use to another Sui Generis use often requires planning permission. Certain sources indicated that permission is only required if the Sui Generis use is materially different from the existing use. 

+*Sui Generis and Planning Permission*+

* The different use classes are set out in the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987. This stipulates that in terms of planning permission, if a use of land is to change within a use class, then this does not require planning permission. However, planning permission is usually needed where the change of use involves activities within the sui generis category. These include theatres, petrol filling stations, casinos, amusement centres, car hire businesses, and so on. See Sui generis for more information.
* There are, however, permitted development rights that allow movement between some sui generis uses and other uses. There is a common misconception that changing the use from an existing use class to a sui generis class always requires planning permission. Permission is only required if the sui generis use is materially different from the existing one.
* If there is any doubt, a lawful development certificate can be applied for. This must include a detailed and unambiguous description of the use, operations or other matter for which it is to be granted. The characteristics of the matter should be spelled out in detail to avoid future problems of interpretation.

{color:#008da6}+*AB SUMMARY OF TICKET*+ {color}

After researching online it seems that Suis Generis has historically been used as the appropriate Use Class for Taxi Businesses. Bolt has currently requested for Use Class e(g)(i) however some Licensors are pushing back on this, it might be worth having a conversation with these Licensors to explain why Use Class e(g)(i) is more suited to Bolts business needs. 

Whilst I appreciate that historically Sui Generis has always been used for Taxi Companies. and this is because Sui Generis is a class of its own and is much wider. It may be that these particular Licensors are not informed on how Bolt operates as a business, they may think that Bolt is like the ‘typical’ Taxi Business (with someone taking bookings at as desk in an office with a fleet of cars outside) this may be why they push back on Use Class e(g)(i). I would suggest liaising with the Licensors that are requesting Sui Generis to try and explain to them that Bolt runs its administrative operations from the offices however the activity takes place elsewhere (given that this is a ride hailing app and differentiates from the ‘normal’ Taxi Business). 

However, in terms of risks to licences with licensing authorities etc, I am not sure where we stand on this point, I have tried to research this online but have not found anything useful. I am not sure if there is correct Use Class Bolt need to use to be validly licensed in that particular local authority. [~accountid:6242fffc1da0e10071388193]/ [~accountid:6017bc19dc29b4006a7f1025] are either of you aware if using a particular Use Class has any adverse effects?

I did tried to debug the issue and below are my findings for the first iteration

+What it the possible root cause?+

 Currently `Duplicate key error` issue are being notice on below endpoints for last 30 days

* `/internal/approveDocument`

* `/internal/uploadDocumentWithFiles`

* `/adminPanel/uploadDocument`

* `/admin/uploadDocument`

* `/internal/changeDocumentTypeOfDocument`

# Error (duplicate key error) is being triggered by the `DocumentTable.updateDocumentByExternalIdInTransaction()`
# Below is the possible root cause for the `duplicate key error`.  Below state examples are for `/internal/approveDocument` endpoint.
## From audit logs and Kibana logs it appears that the endpoint received parallel request at the same point of time but to the different nodes. (In the logs you see n11, n12)
## Approve document request was for the same document id (i.e 81286926). The origin of the request was (172.31.9.227, 172.31.41.246)
## In `DocumentTable.approveDocument()#Line1063` both the request were able to get the transaction instance. But when the request reached Line 1107 it failed to execute.
## This lead to a race condition wherein both the parallel request where trying to change the same document id shared on database level.
## Database acknowledge the constraint the of combine unique key for the individual request.
# Screenshots are attached. Below screenshot are visuals for the description in step 3
## Attachment-2 : Audit logs showing the interaction on the document id by 2 IPS
## Attachment-1: Kibana logs showing the 2 parallel request that the same time for the document id
## Attachment-1.1: More description of the request 1 on node n11
## Attachment-1.2 Description of the request 2 on node n12
## Attachment-4: Logs by the hash id. 
# The same issue (described in step 3) was notice for other endpoints.

+What are possible solutions ?+

# Possible solution:
## One of the possible approach is that we catch the duplicate key error thrown from the database
### then can log it under the different log level
### Also we can send the human readable error as response code for the endpoint
## Have a distributed lock, where the service layer would first check whether the lock exist on table and if not then acquire lock first
### Rather than pros there many cons for this approach.
#### Cons: (slowing the service layer by having additional roundtrip, bottleneck of lock)
## As duplicate keys errors are not much (~ 10 in last 20 days). I would prefer to go with approach 1.

*Background*

For context on this ticket, this Nursery Benefit Scheme was something Ioana was looking at launching alongside the Employee Handbook in the new year for 2023. The Employee Handbook was a holistic guide for new and existing employees to give them and understanding of base rights, procedures and information when joining the UK business. The Employee Handbook is nearly ready to launch, however, it was attached to a series of employee based policies that are still being edited by legal/regs, which may still take a few weeks. The benefit that we can simply launch prior to finalising the Employee Handbook is the Nursery Benefit (if HR wish to continue with this offering to UK employees moving forward).

*Legal review*

The Nursery Benefit TnCs have been approved by legal and its now just down to finalising the claw back addendum and clearing this with tax. Our legal advisors Burness Paull were looking into whether Bolt could have the option to claw back contributions made by Bolt for an Employee if they pay for a substantial amount of the benefit and the Employee leaves the company (this needs tax’s approval). 

Burness Paull our employment specialists have come back to us and suggested an addendum to the original Terms (you will see this on {color:#6554c0}page 60 of the Workplace Nursery Benefit Term{color}s). Their recommended edits to this addendum are as follows:

* _On this basis, you agree to us deducting sums from your final salary or any outstanding payments due to you._  
* _If the value of the costs owed exceed your final salary payment or any outstanding payments due to you, you agree to make payment to the company of any outstanding costs owed within 14 days of the date of the termination of your employment._
* _You agree that if we waive your obligation to repay any costs falling due to the company, you will be solely responsible for any tax that may become payable as a result of said waiver and you shall indemnify the company on a continuing basis in relation to any such tax._

Mike H responded about the DS (a separate chat was created with the ticket requesters + Mike), but looks like DS would be affected after all. He’s waiting for the OPS managers to reply. This is his message:

Do I understand correctly that you would like to remove cash optionality from Acceptance Rate and keep it for Driver Score, meaning that drivers need to accept cash orders but the completion of the cash trips is optional?Generally speaking we should not enforce acceptance rate while completion of trips is optional because this incentivises drivers cancel trips after acceptance. Drivers will accept as many trips as possible to maintain high acceptance rates and then cancel them afterwards without any Driver Score impact. This causes a negative rider experience: more trips are accepted but less are actually completed. Our suggestion is to ensure that whatever drivers accept, should be completed.[Currently 38% of order tries in PL are cash optional|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/looks/20049?qid=xecszcxc9LVN179kT3qRha]. 22% are outside of radius and less than 0.5% are scheduled optional. Here is a description of how optionality works today in Poland;

# If drivers do not accept (or do not respond to) an optional order (for example cash order or outside of driver radius), their *acceptance rate will not decrease.*
# If drivers manually accept an optional order but cancel it after acceptance, their *Driver Score will decrease.*
# If drivers use *the auto-acceptance feature* to accept an optional order and cancel it after acceptance, their *Driver Score will not decrease.*

{quote}On the legal side, having change is the obligation of the driver so it would make sense to punish drivers by lowering their driver’s score.{quote}

Considering this, we should consider first removing optionality entirely from Driver Score and later consider removing cash optionality also from Acceptance Rate.When optionality is removed from Driver Score entirely: drivers can choose to accept or reject optional orders, but if they accept, the order needs to be completed.

# Remains the same as currently.
# Remains the same as currently.
# If drivers use *the auto-acceptance feature* to accept an optional order (eg. cash) and cancel it after acceptance, their *Driver Score will decrease.*

When cash optionality is removed from Acceptance Rate: drivers need to accept and complete cash orders, without exceptions.

# If drivers do not accept (or do not respond to) a cash optional order, their *acceptance rate will decrease.*
# Remains the same as currently
# If drivers use the auto-acceptance feature to accept an optional order (eg. cash) and cancel it after acceptance, their Driver Score will decrease.

Below you may find the *Employment law research for Austria:*

*1. Is the market subject to laws where an employment relationship can be deemed or implied?*

 

No. Whether or not a specific contractual relationship qualifies as an employment contract, a freelance contract or a service contract is assessed on a case by case basis. A service contract would require a specific task already defined at the very beginning. Continuing activities like the ones of drivers therefore do not qualify as a service contract from our point of view. It is therefore likely, that the given distinction will have to be made between employment relationships and a freelance contract. In order to distinguish between such types of contract, the following criteria are applied by authorities and courts:

 

* The contractor can freely choose working times (amount and allocation) and the place of work.
* The contractor is not subject to personal instructions relating to how the work is done (e.g. to wear a specific uniform, how to answer the phone, how to act towards clients, etc.)
* The contractor is allowed to reject individual tasks / orders without having to fear consequences.
* The contractor is allowed to be represented by others and use own employees to provide his services.
* The contractor uses own equipment.
* The contractor is paid on, for example, an hourly basis and especially not paid in case he does not provide services (e.g. due to sickness, because he rejects tasks, etc.) meaning that he bears the economic risk of his activities.
* The contractor is not supervised by the employer and in particular his working times, etc. are not checked. He does not have to participate in internal meetings.

 

Please note that it is not necessary that all criteria are fulfilled. Instead, authorities and courts will assess whether the majority of criteria indicates an employment or a freelance contract. The assessment is based on the practical circumstances, the mere wording of the contract is only of an indicative nature. If the majority of these criteria is not met, the contractual relationship would be considered an employment relationship under Austrian law.

 

*2. Is there any evidence that online platforms/marketplaces are under scrutiny under the legal system (e.g. litigation etc.)?*

 

We are not aware of public statements by authorities or courts that would indicate that they are increasingly taking action against companies in the platform economy. However, it should be noted that new types of employment relationships in particular, such as those of transport service platform drivers or food delivery platform workers, are always getting increased attention not only in society but also in academic research and writing, and this could of course lead to authorities and courts focusing on such companies. Due to the relevance of this issue, there is also a growing number of newspaper articles and headlines dealing with the issues of platform workers (we are referring to headlines such as: “_EU takes action against pseudo self-employment – Workers of online platform companies like Uber, Mjam and Lieferando should get more rights_”; “_Delivery people on two wheels: What does this have to do with freelancers?_”). This could therefore also have an impact on the position of authorities and courts in this respect.

 

Moreover, you will certainly be aware of the various supreme court decisions in other EU Member States such as Germany, Spain, France, the Netherlands, etc., in which divers or food delivery persons in the platform economy are considered to be employed rather than being self-employed. Of course, such decisions are not relevant in Austria, but they are creating a certain trend towards an employment relationship instead of self-employment or freelancing throughout Europe. 

 

There is a very strong cab guild in Austria. This guild takes care to protect classic cabs against competitors such as Uber or Bolt. It is quite possible that this guild is lobbying hard to disrupt competitors in the best possible way.

 

*3. Is the relevant test subject to express presumption criteria?* (_Example: In some jurisdictions, the legislation provides the criteria for the relationship or the agreement concluded between the parties that presume and/or create an employment relationship. For example, in a dispute over the nature of the contract (if the contract has the characteristics of both employment and another contract), the parties are deemed to have an employment relationship unless the employer proves otherwise.)_

 

There are no express presumption criteria. Instead, authorities or courts will base the assessment on the criteria mentioned in question 1. If the majority of the criteria indicate an employment, courts and authorities will assume an employment contract regardless of the parties’ intention.           

 

*4. Are reclassification-sensitive activities (e.g. independent contractors, sole entrepreneurs, drivers, couriers, etc. ) expressly considered by a court or any law to imply an employment relationship?*

 

Not directly. However, if a person, for example, only works for one principal, it might be more difficult to convince authorities that this person is an independent contractor instead of an employee. In such cases it is therefore even more crucial, to ensure that as many criteria as possible indicate a freelance contract.

 

*5. Can claims be made in respect of past periods (i.e. for previously withheld earnings)?*

 

Yes. If a freelance contract is requalified into an employment contract, employees could claim employment related entitlements such as, for example, paid vacation, paid sick leave, remuneration for overtime, minimum salary under the applicable collective bargaining agreement (i.e. assuming that the collective bargaining agreement for the passenger transport industry with passenger cars may be applicable: EUR 1,705 gross per month as of 2023), additional holiday pay (13^th^ salary) and Christmas remuneration (14^th^ salary), etc. The general statute of limitation is three years from the day on which the entitlement became due.

 

In addition to employment related claims, social security authorities could also ask for the social security contributions for at least the last five years. It should be noted that in this case the employer must pay both the employer's and the employee's contributions up to the maximum assessment basis. This amounts to a total of about 40% of the monthly remuneration, capped at a maximum assessment basis of EUR 5,850.00 per month in 2023. If the employee has already paid social security contributions, these payments would have to be credited. Beyond that, however, no recourse can be taken against the employee. In addition, a late payment surcharge of up to EUR 975 per month and interest on arrears of currently 4.63% per year may be added.

 

Further, administrative fines of EUR 730 to EUR 2,180 may be imposed on the managing directors, with the company being liable as well (cf. Section 111 para 2 ASVG). Please note that under certain circumstances, criminal charges may also be imposed.

 

*6. Who is able to take action against Bolt (as an online platform/marketplace for ride-hailing services)? Drivers / group action / regulators?*

 

There are various options. For example, every driver could file an action asking for employment related entitlements. Also, drivers could (anonymously) inform authorities such as the labour inspectorate or social security authorities which can result in inspections. When drivers register for social security as freelancers, they will also get a questionnaire for the purpose of allowing the social security authority to assess whether a freelance contract is actually concluded. Depending on the answers given by drivers, it is also possible that social security authorities come to the conclusion that an employment contract was concluded instead. From experience, the questions are quite tricky and “normal” freelancers do often have difficulties understanding the questions correctly. It is therefore recommended assisting them when answering the questionnaire.

 

In addition, it is also possible that competitors may assert claims under competition law. They could argue that by improperly qualifying drivers as self-employed, Bolt is breaking the law and saving costs. In this case, there is a risk of claims for damages (in theory as it will be difficult to assess an amount of damage) or injunctive relief. For example, the cab guild, which strongly defends the market against other providers, could assert claims under competition law. However, the chances would not be very high if qualification as a freelancer is at least justifiable on the basis of the above criteria.

 

Group actions are not foreseen under Austrian law.

 

*7. Is there any evidence that the authorities have considered independent contractors (e.g. drivers, couriers) eligible for employment benefits in the past (e.g. tax authorities, pension authorities, etc)?*

 

There are currently no decisions on this issue that we are aware of. Please note that only decisions of the Austrian Supreme Court and some decisions of second instance courts are available to the public. It is thus possible that there are already first instance decisions which we are not aware of and have no access to. However, it is also possible that potentially affected companies in general try to avoid any legal disputes and resulting bad public publicity and may therefore settle any claims and damages out of court.

 

*8. What is the level of access to justice in a market (e.g. high state duties, the requirement to have a representative, etc.)?*

 

In proceedings before a civil court, a party must be represented by a lawyer in proceedings before district courts with an amount in dispute of more than EUR 5,000 as well as in proceedings before all higher courts (i.e. regional courts, higher regional courts and the Supreme Court). The general rule in these proceedings is that each party must first bear its own costs. Such costs include: (i) court fees and (ii) legal fees for representation. The actual amount of these fees is based on a certain rate according to the Court Fees Act (_Gerichtsgebührengesetz_) and the Act on Legal Fees (_Rechtsanwaltstarigesetz_) and therefore also depends on the amount in dispute in each case. To give you an idea of the amount of such fees, for example, the court fees for filing an action in proceedings with an amount in dispute of between EUR 3,500 and EUR 7,000 are EUR 335, and for filing an action or a written submission in proceedings with an amount in dispute of between EUR 7,000 and EUR 35,000 are EUR 1,556.00. The legal fees will depend on how many submissions are filed, how many hearings take place, etc. Please note, however, that the party who loses the case entirely must reimburse the other party for all costs incurred. If both parties are only partly successful, the costs are set off against each other (each party pays its own costs) or distributed proportionately (e.g. if one party wins by three quarters, it receives half of its costs).

 

With regard to administrative proceedings (meaning an individual against an authority), there is no obligation for the parties to be represented by a lawyer. The parties may therefore be represented by a lawyer at their own discretion. In the case of an appeal to the Higher Administrative Court or Constitutional Court, the appeal has to be signed by a lawyer. However, the representation by a lawyer in the further proceedings is not necessary. Further, there is no reimbursement of costs in the first and second instance administrative proceedings and only limited before the Higher Administrative Court. Therefore, each party has to bear its own costs.

 

*9. Can claims be made to reclassify all drivers/couriers of the platform in a market at once?*

 

Yes, if for example a social security authority carries out inspections and comes to the conclusion that one of the drivers is an employee, it is very likely that all other drivers will be subject to inspections as well and – if the situation is the same – it is also very likely that the assessment of the social security authorities will be the same.

Our {{chat}}endpoints comply with the overall auth convention. All endpoints use so called “StandardRequest” dedicated for certain vertical

* [DeliveryCourierApp.StandardRequest|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d5efed43b95f3c871d17ba0bd0ffc4315a079dae/common/delivery/app/DeliveryCourierApp.ts#L14]
* [DeliveryClientApp.StandardRequest|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d5efed43b95f3c871d17ba0bd0ffc4315a079dae/common/delivery/app/DeliveryClientApp.ts]
* [DriverApp.StandardRequest|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/947d9f1fec2ddcc716270715cd7cd340ff2d7a2f/common/driver/app/DriverApp.ts#L4]
* [ClientApp.StandardRequest|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/947d9f1fec2ddcc716270715cd7cd340ff2d7a2f/common/user/app/ClientApp.ts]

Unfortunately, CourierApp’s variables are defined in different case (snake_case instead of camelCase) than other apps. 



In order to override [DeliveryCourierApp.StandardRequest|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d5efed43b95f3c871d17ba0bd0ffc4315a079dae/common/delivery/app/DeliveryCourierApp.ts#L14] with some our custom request, we’d need to define our custom auth strategy. These are grouped into FirstParty and ThirdParty auth types. 

* External auth strategies are more flexible and free to implement in desired way.
* Internal ones, have their limitations BUT they cover all necessary token validations per vertical.


I tried both approaches:

* Internal auth bases theoretically lets me create a custom request interface and use it in custom auth strategy. However, it fails at the api generation stage - it requires either the StandardRequest or empty request. I found no way to overcome it.
* External auth is more flexible, but I’d need to copy-paste the whole implementation for generic token validation for courier (and I’m not sure if that would work). Extracting the generic part of the library and adjusting tiny for us to support and maintain afterwards seems like an overkill.



That tasks is much more complex than it might sound like. We decided to implement it at mobile end and comply with standard authorization methods used across Bolt.

Here is the Mixpanel Dashboard that shows conversion from {{Call Driver Inapp Tap}} to {{Call Finished}}: [https://mixpanel.com/s/2yMX3d|https://mixpanel.com/s/2yMX3d|smart-link] 

There are two events:

* {{Call Driver Inapp Tap}} that is logged when user taps a VoIP call button from the contact option menu. This event has a parameter {{origin}} that represents where this menu was shown (active ride or after ride).
* {{Call Finished}} that is logged when we received from Sinch an event that the call was finished and it says what was the reason for the ending a call (hung up, timeout, error, etc.).

These events can be linked one to another by a certain order handle ({{order_id}} + {{city_id}}). This is what {{hold constant}} does in Mixpanel. 

So my hypothesis was that I can get the necessary data if I build two funnels (conversion from one event to another): {{Call Driver Inapp Tap}} -> {{Call Finished}} where in the first funnel {{origin}} will include all active order entry points and the second - only {{History}}. Then in {{Call Finished}} I could just include the calls ended with unsuccessful reasons caused by not accepting the call on the other end (eg. Timeout, Denied or No Answer).

However the interpretation of these Mixpanel dashboards is questionable. When I tried to invert the results (see how many calls were ended successfully during an active order vs post-order calls) it shows that there are about 1% successfully ended calls if they started from the active order {{origin}} which can’t be true. So maybe I’m using the Mixpanel tooling wrongly.

_Article 33a 2a: The requirement to submit documents referred to in paragraph 2 subparagraph 1 by the taxable person is also considered to be fulfilled in the case where the taxable person submits statements of the same content._

_Article 33a 3: The condition of presenting the documents referred to in paragraph 2, subparagraph 1 shall not apply if the head of the customs and fiscal office is in possession of updated documents submitted by the taxable person._

To accommodate the requirements and data quality we have (assuming even if PO adds gateway info for paypal, we still might introduce instrument for overcapture in the future that doesn’t have gateway info enabled at first) we can for example:

{noformat}{
    "overcapture_enabled": true,
    "overcapture_disabled_for_countries": [
        "gb",
        "za",
        "ng",
        "ge"
    ],
    "overcapture_enabled_for_instruments": [
       {"instrument_type": "adyen_paypal", "limit_type": "global"},
       {"instrument_type":"applepay", "limit_type": "gateway"},
       {"instrument_type":"googlepay", "limit_type": "gateway"},
       {"instrument_type":"processout", "limit_type": "gateway"},
    ],
    "overcapture_percent_limit": 20,
    "overcapture_gateways_percent_limit": [
       {"gateway_name": "adyen", "percent_limit": 15},
       {"gateway_name": "paystack", "percent_limit": 5},
       {"gateway_name": "payupaymentos", "percent_limit": 30}
    ]
}{noformat}

With the following semantics:

* {{overcapture_enabled}} :feature flag switch, if false there will be no overcaptures attempted at all
* {{overcapture_disabled_for_countries}}  : if payment is one of those countries then the overcapture will not be attempted
*  {{overcapture_enabled_for_instruments}} : if payment instrument type is one of the listed then the overcapture will be attempted using either “global” or “gateway” overcapture limit type check, ie..
** if “global” then the {{overcapture_percent_limit}} will be used as overcapture limit check
** if “gateway” then the  {{overcapture_gateways_percent_limit}}  will be used as overcapture limit check
* {{overcapture_gateways_percent_limit}} : if payment has a gateway info attached/available then the specific gateway percent_limit check will be used (e.g. for  {{"paystack"}} it will be 5%) 
** [?] if there is no gateway specific overcapture limit for the gateway_name available in the payment then the global {{overcapture_percent_limit}} will be used
** [?] if there is no   gateway_name available in the payment  then the global {{overcapture_percent_limit}} will be used (or we can skip the overcapture in this case, or we can use the minimum of all gateways - because in fact it’s one of them)

For the last 2 points (marked with [?]) checking with Rodolfo what semantics we should go for in those edge cases.

I’ve created a PoC error decorator for the {{/getDropoffData}}. [Draft PR here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/68959]. It demonstrates that such decorator can be added to the existing code in a minimally intrusive way (using {{Promise.catch()}} chaining).

The PoC also highlights a few non-code things:

* The data on the errors in the tables does not translate well into code. The problem is with errors that have multiple numerical codes per name ({{USER_NOT_FOUND}}, {{USER_BLOCKED}}, etc.). For example, {{USER_BLOCKED = 16600}} is defined in the code of Delivery vertical. Do we ever get _this specific code_ in {{/getDropoffData}}? I highly doubt that. But the tables only say {{USER_BLOCKED}} is thrown by {{/getDropoffData}}, not which one of them.
* Also, some of these multi-code errors _do_ have a translatable message already at the point of origin. So we really need to adjust the data to see which ones are in the scope for this investigation and which are not.
* Also, there’s a list of errors that are _excluded_ from the reporting: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/integration/gateway/main/Bootstrap.ts#L171|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/integration/gateway/main/Bootstrap.ts#L171] Their presence in the table is very confusing. 
* Simply repeating the error code names as translatable strings does not bring a lot of benefit for the user. E.g., “User Blocked” might be somewhat informative, but it is not actionable. “Server Error” is not informative at all. So a deeper investigation is needed for each error just to understand the semantics and compose a meaningful message string.
* Some of the errors (Geo “polygon” errors) look like they should be converted to non-error states (in the {{gateway}}, not at the source). They are not meaningful (to the user), not actionable, and I see them explicitly listed as "OK errors" in other parts of the code.

Hi [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] ,

I am no French law expert but do we could dig deeper into this matter if needed. Please flag if you require a full legal analysis for relevant activities in the French market e.g. bolt academy, branded cars etc.

For your info, I did a quick search and on ‘demarcharge abusif’ (i.e. unsolicited communication or spam calls) which is regulated under   French consumer protection laws (e.g. LOI n° 2020-901 du 24 juillet 2020 ).



In a nutshell, demarchage abusif falls under the scope of  communications made for commercial purposes towards consumers who have not consented to receiving such communications. In certain instances, this can be considered abusive/unflawful if specific criteria are not met. For instance, calls made from mobile numbers 06 - 07 should be restricted to interpersonal communications, no caller ID calls are forbidden, communication is only allowed during specific hours etc.

It is unlikely that calling a driver in connection to the provision of their services with Bolt to be considered a unlawful under French laws. There seems to be an exception that allows calls in relation to a signed contract between the caller and the consumer.

Once again, please advise if specialist support required to provide a conclusive opinion as this is just high-level info.

Best,

Anthi

I have not heard of any such conflict in Romania.

When it comes to the relationship between fleets and couriers, there are several types of employment contracts that fleets can conclude with their couriers:

* Individual employment contract for an indefinite period;
* Individual fixed-term employment contract;

—--

* Full time contract
* Part-time contract

Also, the _Civil Code_ allows collaboration contracts, as follows:

* collaboration contract with withholding tax
* copyright agreement
* service contract

Collaboration contracts can be concluded with:

* individuals who earn income from independent activities: income from copyrights, liberal professions (lawyer, doctor, nurse, financial consultant, etc.)
* PFA (natural authorised person), PFI, II, IF, SRL (limited liability company)

Hi [~accountid:61542c1cd9820f00705c38bb] 

as for the payment card details, I can confirm that this wouldn’t be disclosed given PCI DSS requirements.

As for the general data sharing framework, this approach is not aligned with our legal interpretation of this matter. We strongly believe that given the overall contractual set up, in case of any regulatory intervention, the partner could still be deemed a data controller (and not a processor), however the risk associated with that is mostly on partner’s side.

In this specific scenario, given that (a) the Partner clearly has very different interpretation of the set up; and (b) it results in overall medium risk for Bolt, from privacy side we can agree to proceed with proposed framework. However please note that this would translate to different risk profile than with our standard model. As already mentioned in this ticket, this includes the following risks:

* Bolt would be responsible for the processing carried out by the Partner in the course of this agreement (Bolt could seek redress from the partner, however it would be ultimately the liable entity and the process of proving damages for data protection-related matters is usually very difficult), that includes any GDPR infringements committed by the Partner in connection with this agreement;
* data protection complaints/requests from the data subjects lodged by the end-users ;
* the Partner can be audited by Bolt (as set out in the GDPR and proposed contract), it should also inform Bolt about any incidents related to the processed personal data.

Please confirm if this change and proposed terms are acceptable from the business perspective, otherwise I’d kindly ask our partner to provide more detailed rationale of their position as it hasn’t been expressed so far in the e-mail thread.

{noformat}drop table billing_transaction;

create table billing_transaction
(
    id                      bigint unsigned auto_increment
        primary key,
    created                 timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP not null,
    last_update             timestamp default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP not null on update CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    source_id               bigint                              not null,
    source_type             varchar(100)                        not null,
    group_source_type       varchar(100)                        null,
    source_city_id          int                                 null,
    source_group_id         bigint                              null,
    target_account_type     varchar(255)                        not null,
    target_account_id       bigint                              not null,
    transaction_reason_type varchar(45)                         not null,
    is_active               tinyint(1)                          null,
    country_code            varchar(2)                          not null,
    business_line           varchar(32)                         null,
    constraint transaction_group_key_idx
        unique (target_account_id, target_account_type, transaction_reason_type, is_active, source_type,
                source_group_id, source_city_id, source_id),
    constraint transaction_idempotency_idx
        unique (source_id, source_type, source_city_id, target_account_type, target_account_id, transaction_reason_type,
                is_active)
);


-- Set the delimiter to use a custom delimiter
DELIMITER //

-- Create a stored procedure to generate inserts
CREATE PROCEDURE generate_inserts()
BEGIN
    DECLARE i INT DEFAULT 0;

    WHILE i < 10000 DO
            SET i = i + 1;

            INSERT INTO billing_transaction (
                created, last_update, source_id, source_type, group_source_type,
                source_city_id, source_group_id, target_account_type, target_account_id,
                transaction_reason_type, is_active, country_code, business_line
            )
            SELECT
                        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                        FLOOR(RAND() * 1000000) AS source_id, 'source_type' AS source_type,
                        IF(RAND() < 0.25, 'group_source_type', null) AS group_source_type,
                        FLOOR(RAND() * 1000) AS source_city_id,
                        IF(RAND() < 0.5, FLOOR(RAND() * 1000000), NULL) AS source_group_id,
                        'target_account_type' AS target_account_type,
                        FLOOR(RAND() * 1000000) AS target_account_id,
                        'transaction_reason_type' AS transaction_reason_type,
                        FLOOR(RAND() * 2) AS is_active, 'cc' AS country_code,
                        'business_line' AS business_line
            FROM DUAL
            LIMIT 1;
        END WHILE;
END //

-- Reset the delimiter back to the default
DELIMITER ;

-- Call the stored procedure to generate inserts
CALL generate_inserts();




DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS generate_inserts;

Hello, good afternoon. I trust you’re doing very well.

Services provided to VAT taxpayers established within the European Union are regarded to be supplied in the country where the service’s recipient is established for VAT purposes, irrespective of the place where the service’s provider is established.

Therefore, in the case at hand, services provided by a company based in Israel will be regarded to be supplied in Estonia if the service is addressed to Bolt Operations OÜ. This company will be liable to settle EE VAT under the reverse charge mechanism.

This rule applies although the service provided by the Israeli company is related to the narrative of a tender taking place out of EE, as long as the service’s recipient is Bolt Ops. In this regard, please bear in mind that Bolt Ops OÜ provides micro-mobility rental services in most of the EU countries where we operate under the cross-border business model.

In line with the above, services related to the narrative of tenders taking place in countries where we provide micro-mobility rental services under the localized business model (UA, HR, PT, IE, SI and MT) should be addressed to the Bolt local company that provides these rental services. Therefore, for instance, if the service is related to a tender taking place in Portugal, the service should be invoiced to Bolt Support Services PT, Unipessoal Lda, and this company will be liable to settle PT VAT under the reverse charge mechanism.

Should you require further information or any clarification, please let me know.

Thank you and have a good day.

As general recommendation local teams are encouraged to think how to educate local users to detect fraud. There is no universal/global way to deliver local awareness as we work in som many different markets and local teams know best what messages work in the region. I have seen (too) many failed EU global security awareness rising programs because they target only average western europeans (whoever this may be …) and would like to avoid launching yet-another similar program. h3. *List of limitations:*

*Geospatial Android Min API:*
Geospatial API uses ARCore library and Android API 24 is the minimum since ARCore only works with 24 and higher.

*Geospatial Hardware:*
For the Geospatial API, one of the key pieces of hardware required is a magnetometer that meets the Geospatial API specifications. Some magnetometers do not meet the spec; devices with these off-spec magnetometers are not supported. List of supported devices: [https://developers.google.com/ar/devices|https://developers.google.com/ar/devices|smart-link] 

*Geospatial API usage quota:*
We need to check our analytics how many rides globaly finished per minute. The ARCore SDK limits API requests to the ARCore service to the following limits for each project that uses the ARCore SDK:
*1,000 sessions started per minute, or*
*100,000 requests per minute*

h3. List of possibilities:

* [Increase user location position accuracy|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~624edb164fe01d006bab4a42/pages/4382261860/Visual+Positioning+System+VPS+investigation#Real-case-PoC-to-calculate-position-of-the-scooter-instead-of-camera] using Geospatial API
* Retrive frames to post-proccess extracted picture as the finish ride picture and for parking quality AI check

h3. Conclusion:

VPS feature should be shipped as Dynamic feature to not increase initial installation app size in Google Play, because of adding new libraries & dependencies.
It's better to divide feature development on several phrases, because of overall feature complexity and different tech (VPS, ML object detection, etc), for example:

* Phase 1: use VPS user location for finish ride flow
* Phase 2: detect objects (scooters) and calculate scooter position
* Phase 3: adding AR object to show parking places.

The agreement states that damages must be reported to Det Grønne Autohus and scratches will be settled upon return of the van, as mentioned by you. 

Firstly, I would want to clarify if any insurance was signed for this lease? It sounds like only the Lessor (Det Grønne Autohus) has insurance in place and if such insurance doesn’t cover the damage then Bolt will be held liable. Regarding the scratches we could argue that they shall be paid once the vehicle is returned, if this is beneficial from a business perspective. 

Regarding the replacement van, did we sign a separate lease for this van? Do we have any documentation around it? If we don’t have an agreement for this then it could be deemed that it should be covered by the same agreement and that it should act as the original vehicles for the period that the van was replaced. It will be difficult to argue against liability for damages in such a case. It will be difficult to argue that the cost would not have arisen if the other van was working as 1) looking at our track record here we seem to damage the cars heavily in a short time so additional damages to the original car are not unlikely and 2) it is common practice that you are responsible for damages of the vehicles you lease unless it is agreed otherwise in the agreement, even if it is a replacement vehicle (such damages would have likely occurred on the original vehicle if we had used the vehicle the same way during that period). 

However, it is the lessor that bears the burden of proof that Bolt has indeed damaged the car to the extent claimed. Are there any damages that could be challenged, e.g. pre-existing damages or scratches?

I think that I figured out the reasoning for different flows - in the regular case we are generating the {{RIDER_CAMPAIGN}} record from Bolt to the rider because Bolt directly provides the discount. In the netted case the driver provides the discount and Bolt compensates the driver for it. Hence the {{RIDER_CAMPAIGN}} record is from the driver to the rider and there is this {{RIDER_CAMPAIGN_COMPENSATION}} record from Bolt to the driver.

In addition to that the latter ({{RIDER_CAMPAIGN_COMPENSATION}} record) also exists between Bolt and the driver in case of cash rides.

To be honest from my perspective I would leave the flows as they are as they represent the actual flows. But I guess it’s good to double check with accounting and DWH. 🙂

Hi [~accountid:633be2c588ed2ebef97dd442] and [~accountid:5f7722e0287870006a0b433e],

After receiving opinions from external lawyers regarding specific situation we have come to conclusion that legally employees from Baltic states who are temporarily sent to work in Bolt Germany are considered as posted employees. We do not see any options to change that by changing the duration or frequency of the stays.

If the employer decides to disregard posted employees’ regulations and use instead a business trip approach:

* the German supervisory authority may apply supervisory measures under German law. Non-compliance with the rules of the Posted Workers Act (_Arbeitnehmer-Entsendegesetz, AEntG_) can result in administrative fines of up to EUR 500.000 for the person commissioning the work and/or the contractor.
* In case more favourable German law provisions should be applied to the employees compared to Estonian, Latvian or Lithuanian law, the employees may demand the application of respective terms and conditions as well as file claims against the employer (including for unpaid salary, leaves not granted etc.).

Taking into account mentioned I see 2 options how to continue:

# Sending Baltic state employees to Germany under posting of employees rules, meaning that German mandatory working conditions would be applicable (most probably they still will not be able to work during night time and on weekends) + there will be obligation to inform respective state institutions in Germany about posting of employees prior to the posting.
# Stop sending Baltic state employees to Germany and recruit local German Vehicle specialists who will do the job and/or cover this need using external service providers in Germany.

[^Agreement_Bolt Services DE_DDS Bagnut B.V._01.07.2023_scanned.pdf]

What I mean by “temporary campaign” is not to grant full discounts or full refunds for intercity rides indefinitely, without any time limit. For instance, we should not keep on granting these discounts or refunds once the fleet in the “target city” (i.e., Kaunas) has reached a significant amount or the number of vehicles that we need in that city. But the “campaign” should not extend beyond a reasonable time to reach the goals set in the business case.

The NATO summit is a very good business reason to kick off this campaign and keep it until the summit is over, and perhaps until the end of summer. Thinking out loud, a good business reason might be to run the campaign until the end of summer to encourage the use of Bolt Drive cars for vacation rides.

Bearing in mind that we can’t forecast how many vehicles may be needed in cities where we do not provide car-sharing services yet in order to cover the demand for our car-sharing service, the business case should explain that an affordable way to take Bolt Drive cars to those cities and, this way, to start gathering information to analyze whether or not those new markets can be profitable is by allowing users based in Vilnius to use Bolt Drive cars for intercity rides for a very low cost.

In line with such an idea, the information that you shared is a very good way to support the idea above, because it shows how much money we might save by putting in place the campaign.

Another good reason to support the campaign would be that its scope would be limited ONLY to rides from Vilnius to new market cities (Kaunas and/or Klaipeda), but not the other way around. So, the low-cost rides should not be allowed for rides from Kaunas and/or Klaipeda to Vilnius, as this is a city where the largest fleet of Bolt Drive cars is already stationed.

I don’t know what “rebalancing cars” is, so I’m afraid I cannot help in this regard. If you let me know what it is, perhaps I can try to come up with some other ideas to support the business plan.

Thanks! Have a good day.

*New Query*

{noformat}SELECT
    'apple_search_ads' AS channel_name,
    '' AS account_id,
    CAST(campaign_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS campaign_id,
    CAST(adgroup_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS adgroup_id,
    CAST(ad_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS ad_id,
    ad_name,
    ad_updated_time,
    adgroup_name,
    adgroup_updated_time,
    campaign_name || ' || ' || 'ios' || ' || ' || 'search' as campaign_name,
    campaign_updated_time
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        ad_id,
        ad_name,
        adgroup_id AS adgroup_id,
        ad_updated_time::timestamp
    FROM
        (
            SELECT
                id AS ad_id,
                ad_group_id AS adgroup_id,
                text AS ad_name,
                modification_time AS ad_updated_time,
                rank() over (PARTITION by id ORDER BY modification_time DESC) AS is_latest
            FROM ng_apple_search_ads_spark.keyword_history kwh
        )
    WHERE is_latest = 1
) AS kw_info
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        DISTINCT campaign_id,
        adgroup_id,
        adgroup_name,
        adgroup_updated_time::timestamp
    FROM
        (
            SELECT
                id AS adgroup_id,
                campaign_id,
                name AS adgroup_name,
                modification_time AS adgroup_updated_time,
                rank() over (PARTITION by id ORDER BY modification_time DESC) AS is_latest
            FROM ng_apple_search_ads_spark.ad_group_history agh
        )
    WHERE is_latest = 1
) AS adgroup_info USING (adgroup_id)
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        campaign_id,
        campaign_name,
        campaign_updated_time::timestamp
    FROM (
            SELECT
                id AS campaign_id,
                name AS campaign_name,
                modification_time AS campaign_updated_time,
                rank() over (PARTITION by id ORDER BY modification_time DESC) AS is_latest
            FROM ng_apple_search_ads_spark.campaign_history ch
        )
    WHERE is_latest = 1
) AS campaign_info USING (campaign_id)

UNION ALL

SELECT DISTINCT 
    'apple_search_ads' AS channel_name,
    NULL AS account_id,
    cast(campaign_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS campaign_id,
    'c_' || cast(campaign_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS adgroup_id,
    'c_' || cast(campaign_id AS VARCHAR(50)) AS ad_id,
    '' AS ad_name,
    campaign_updated_time AS ad_updated_time,
    '' AS adgroup_name,
    campaign_updated_time AS adgroup_updated_time,
    campaign_name || ' || ' || 'ios' || ' || ' || 'search' as campaign_name,
    campaign_updated_time
FROM (
    SELECT
        id AS campaign_id,
        name AS campaign_name,
        modification_time AS campaign_updated_time,
        rank() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY modification_time DESC) AS is_latest
    FROM ng_apple_search_ads_spark.campaign_history ch
    -- DOING THE UNION TO GET CAMPAIGNS FILTERED BY THIS LINE
    WHERE id NOT IN (
        SELECT campaign_id
        FROM ng_apple_search_ads_spark.keyword_history
    )
)
WHERE is_latest = 1
{noformat}

* Always COMPUTATION_TYPE=“EXCLUSIVE” _(previously was “INCLUSIVE”)_

* TOTAL_VAT = 15% of “Vatable amount”
* TOTAL_AMOUNT = “Vatable amount” + TOTAL_VAT _(previously was “Vatable amount”)_
* TOTAL_LEVY = sum of levies (item_list.LEVY_AMOUNT_A + item_list.LEVY_AMOUNT_B + item_list.LEVY_AMOUNT_C, all without VAT)

Hey [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e], answering your questions below:

* So basically we must review the suspicious accounts?

This would be a more cautious approach. However, if we are absolutely sure that this is fraud (and can prove it), then we can block the driver or the fleet immediately if the driver / fleet has been caught doing this several times (and we have evidence of this). If this is the first time, then we need to notify the driver / fleet of the permanent block at least 30 days in advance.

Less cautious approach is to block driver / fleet permanently immediately. The difference stems from the fact that there is no 100% clarity as to whether such actions are in breach of the local laws in each market or this is just a breach of our T&Cs. The research on that would be quite lengthy, and I do not consider it necessary at this stage. The risks of going forward with the less cautious approach are not very high.

*In any case we need to provide driver / fleet with the reasons for block and let them know that they have a right to appeal the decision.*

* For all countries or some of them?

I am largely relying on EU regulation while advising on this matter. So this applies to the EU markets. However, if possible, I would advise implementing the same unified approach in all markets. Otherwise, we need to go country by country to map out what are the rules specific to a certain country.

* Can we take automatic blocking decisions when we are sure it’s fraudulent behaviour?

This should be cross-checked with the privacy team (cc [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18]). If there are no obstacles to do that from privacy perspective, then we need to add a clause on that to our T&Cs.

Also, if there is no repetitive fraud, then we need to provide reasoning to the drivers / fleets. If there is a repetitive fraud, then no need to provide reasons.

* For temporary or permanent block?

Both, considering the above.

*user_creation_ip*

{code:sql}WITH stats AS (
WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
d.meta.city_id AS city_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.user.creation_ip') AS creation_ip
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT 
i.creation_ip AS creation_ip, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_state = 'cancelled' AND etl.user_price > 0 THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_cancellation_fee_rides,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN (etl.is_payment_problem OR etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_final_failed_payment) THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_bad_payment_rides,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_try_state = 'finished' THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_finished_rides
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id
WHERE 
etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
(
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_state = 'cancelled' AND etl.user_price > 0 THEN etl.order_id END) > 1 
OR 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_try_state = 'finished' THEN etl.order_id END) > 1
)
)
SELECT u.user_creation_ip AS KEY, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) AS week_users_created, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) AS month_week_users_created,
s.count_cancellation_fee_rides,
s.count_bad_payment_rides,
s.count_finished_rides
FROM ng_pii.fraud_user AS u
JOIN stats AS s ON u.user_creation_ip = s.creation_ip
WHERE 
u.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND u.user_creation_ip IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1,4,5,6
HAVING 
(
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) > 3
OR
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) > 10
)
AND
(
s.count_bad_payment_rides > 10
OR 
s.count_cancellation_fee_rides > 10 
)
ORDER BY 2 DESC
LIMIT 9999{code}
